messages:
Maya SRE: FYI - seeing a spike in SSE disconnects from na-east starting ~06:20 UTC. Multiple customers report partial streams (last chunk missing) + client reconnect loops. Dash shows 5xx stream errors jump from 0.2% -> 4.6% over 10m. https://metrics.redwood.ai/streams?range=15m :eyes:

Devon Support: Which API path? is this the regular /v1/streams or the new multiplexing endpoint? any auth errors or billing rpcs showing?

Maya SRE: Mostly /v1/streams (text-generation streaming). No billing errors seen. A handful of token-expiry warnings but majority are upstream resets / stream truncated. Example repro (dev environment):

```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-alpha"
```

Client sees: last event stops mid-response, then `ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR` on reconnect attempt. Server logs around the time show repeated lines like:
```
[06:22:11] stream_out: write failed: broken pipe
[06:22:11] sse_chunk: truncated_write: expected=4096 got=1780
[06:22:11] upstream: reset by peer (code=104)
```

Liam Infra: We had a kernel netdev update rolled at 06:12 UTC in na-east to address packet loss on the host pool. Roll was targeted but looks like a larger blast radius. Packet retransmits + small window size could cause fragmented SSE frames from our proxy -> runtime path. I'm seeing increased RSTs from the proxy layer.

Priya PM: Customer-facing impact? anyone triaged customers that reported production incidents?

Devon Support: On a quick scan, 3 paying customers reported app-level errors (chat windows dropping mid-message). I've opened tickets with repro logs. Marking P2 until we confirm scope.

Maya SRE: Repro steps for eng: 1) open streaming SSE via curl above, 2) send a prompt that generates ~1.5k tokens so multiple chunks are emitted, 3) observe mid-stream stop. Also captured tcpdump showing sequence of small fragmented packets coinciding with `truncated_write` in server. Attaching excerpt to ticket.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] service=stream-proxy region=na-east increased_5xx=+420% window=10m

Liam Infra: Immediate mitigation options:
- roll back kernel netdev change on affected hosts (fast but requires host drains)
- route new streaming sessions to na-central/na-west via traffic steering (no client creds change, just routing)
- force non-streaming fallback for affected tenants (application-level change; sends completed responses as single REST payload)
- increase keepalive and disable proxy `proxy_buffering` for SSE paths to avoid fragmentation reassembly issues

Maya SRE: I'll try routing new sessions away from na-east for a canary first, that should cut user impact in half. Can we push a routing override?

Liam Infra: Yes, setting route policy now: `route.streams.region_preference = [na-central, na-west]` for new sessions. Old sessions remain on their origin. Doing gradual shift starting +2m.

Priya PM: Please also draft a status page blurb we can post. Suggested: "We are investigating intermittent streaming disruptions in our NA-East region. Some streaming responses may be truncated; we are routing new traffic to alternate regions and working on a full remediation."

Maya SRE: Draft posted to #status-drafts, pinging @statusbot to publish once we have mitigation confirmed. :thumbsup:

Devon Support: Quick customer workaround to share: call the non-streaming endpoint (`/v1/completions` or `?stream=false`) to receive whole responses until we clear this. Also recommend retry logic for clients to perform an idempotent reconnect and request restarts.

Maya SRE: I'm also temporarily increasing signed token TTL for internal test clients — token expiry wasn't root cause but it reduces noise while we confirm.

Liam Infra: Rolling back netdev patch now on subset of hosts (batch 1/4). ETA 8m. If rollback restores stable 5xx rate -> promote rollback to remaining hosts.

Devon Support: I'm updating the open tickets with the fallback workaround and routing note.

Maya SRE: After reroute started, error rate dropped ~60% in 6m. Still seeing occasional partials from long-lived sessions that were pinned to na-east. Will drain those hosts after rollback finishes.

Liam Infra: Rollback batch 1 verified, 5xxs back down to baseline on those hosts. Proceeding with batches 2-4.

deploy-bot: [INFO] rollback_complete service=host-netdev region=na-east batch=1

Maya SRE: Status update to publish: "Mitigated: We observed and mitigated intermittent streaming truncation in NA-East. A kernel netdev change caused fragmented packets leading to truncated SSE chunks. Traffic for new streaming sessions was routed to alternate regions and the offending kernel change was rolled back. Ongoing: draining/restarting affected hosts and follow-up RCA. Customers can use the non-streaming endpoint as a temporary workaround."

statusbot: Posted to status.redwood.ai - Incident #INC-2026-1823456789 published (mitigated).

Priya PM: Good job. Can ops prepare an RCA doc and a short engineer-facing blameless postmortem with the exact kernel commit id and host list? I'll coordinate customer comms for those who escalated.

Maya SRE: Will create RCA in /confluence/incidents/INC-2026-1823456789 and include tests to validate SSE chunking under kernel-level fragmentation (tcpdump + synthetic stream tests). Action items:
- Maya: create RCA + repro harness (ETA EOD)
- Liam: list of hosts & kernel commit ids + patch PR for safer rollout gating (ETA today)
- Devon: customer comms draft + ticket updates (ETA 2h)

Devon Support: Adding follow-up note: suggest adding runtime-level sanity check that validates SSE chunk sizes and gracefully falls back to completed responses if fragmentation detected repeatedly per session.

Maya SRE: Agreed. Adding a short-term fix: if we detect >3 truncated chunks in a session, switch that session to non-streaming automatically and log diagnostic blob for RCA.

Liam Infra: Closing loop: final rollback finished at 06:47 UTC, all regions within normal error bands by 06:50. Marking incident mitigated but keeping channel open for RCA prep.

Maya SRE: incident status -> MITIGATED. Closing thread once RCA doc is linked. :white_check_mark:
